html:
SMTO-LLM-0071 — Stop failed

GUID: 7b679a38-adeb-5c63-a125-08d97bf103b1
Slug: local-ai-stop-failed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO told the model server to stop, but it hadn't shut down a couple of seconds later. It may still be closing, or it may still be running.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait about a minute, then in a new message ask SMTO to show the details of that model server on the Gateway. Large model servers can take longer than SMTO waited to shut down, so a later look shows whether it finished.
  2. If it shows as stopped or exited, you can start it again or start a different one. Once the old server is gone, a new one won't clash with it over the port or graphics card.
  3. If it still shows as running or unknown, ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to check and stop it there. A server that ignores the stop request needs someone on that computer to deal with it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the model server as stopped or exited.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't start a replacement model server until the old one is confirmed stopped.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway sent a stop to an SMTO-managed Local AI runtime but could not confirm the process exited within its wait, so the stop's effect is unknown.

What this means

  • The owned-process stop path could not establish termination within its wait; the resulting receipt may retain unknown effects. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The owned-process stop path could not establish termination within its wait; the resulting receipt may retain unknown effects.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original process identity and runtime receipt, including any surviving process group.

How to fix it

  • The owned process group did not exit within the 2-second wait after the stop signal; inspect the runtime (local_ai.runtime / runtimes) and the host's process list for that process group until it is conclusively exited. Do not start or restart a replacement for the same profile while termination is uncertain, and do not select a process by port.
  • Reconcile the owned runtime with the Gateway operator; do not issue a replacement start while termination remains uncertain.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • The original owned runtime is conclusively inactive before replacement.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
